domain_label: Erotetic Logic & Question Semantics (Question Science subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
analysis is purely logical and linguistic, with neutral informational framing; no domain-specific answer content is asserted
a context / common ground is available against which presuppositions are evaluated
questions are analyzed at the level of logical form, abstracting from speaker intention beyond encoded bias
exclusions: deciding the actual true answer to any object-level question (only answerhood conditions are analyzed)
speech-act force and politeness beyond encoded bias
rhetorical questions whose function is assertion rather than inquiry
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for erotetic-logic and question-semantics work units, informed by the logic of questions and answers, partition semantics, inferential erotetic logic, and Question-Under-Discussion pragmatics; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Belnap & Steel 1976 The Logic of Questions and Answers; Hamblin 1958 Questions; Groenendijk & Stokhof 1984 Studies on the Semantics of Questions and the Pragmatics of Answers (partition semantics); Wisniewski 1995 The Posing of Questions and 2013 Questions, Inferences, and Scenarios (inferential erotetic logic); Roberts 1996 Information Structure in Discourse (Question Under Discussion); van Fraassen 1980 The Scientific Image (why-questions and contrast classes)

competency_questions.question: How is a question's logical type (polar, alternative, wh) recognized and what answer space does each fix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QTYPE_POLAR, QTYPE_ALT and QTYPE_WH classify the type and fix its answer space

competency_questions.question: How are wh, alternative, and why questions distinguished and what do their answers instantiate (instances, options, or explanantia)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QTYPE_WH/QTYPE_ALT instantiate variables/options; QTYPE_WHY requests an explanans over a contrast class

competency_questions.question: What does a question presuppose and how are existential/uniqueness and explanandum presuppositions extracted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRESUPPOSITION extracts the common entailment of direct answers; QTYPE_WHY fixes the explanandum

competency_questions.question: How is a false or loaded presupposition detected and why is such a question flagged rather than answered, and how is encoded bias separated from a hard presupposition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FALSE_PRESUP flags a presupposition false-in-context; NEGATIVE_QUESTION separates bias from presupposition

competency_questions.question: What is the answerhood condition: what counts as an answer, and how does the QUD constrain felicitous answers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANSWERHOOD fixes the resolving-proposition criterion; QUD constrains relevance

competency_questions.question: How is the set of direct answers constructed and what makes each direct answer canonical and minimal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIRECT_ANSWER builds the canonical minimal answers covering each issue cell

competency_questions.question: How are complete vs partial and mention-some vs mention-all answers distinguished and the right adequacy bar set?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLETE_ANSWER sets the exhaustivity reading and the complete/partial boundary

competency_questions.question: How does partition semantics model a question and tie exhaustive answers to blocks of logical space?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PARTITION_SEM models the question as an equivalence relation whose blocks are exhaustive answers

competency_questions.question: How is the admissible answer set computed for closed question types and decided by membership?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADMISSIBLE_SET enumerates permitted answers for polar/alternative and decides replies by membership

competency_questions.question: How is type-conformance checked for open-type answers and when is a reply category-mismatched?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TYPE_CONFORMANCE checks the sortal/category match of an open-type answer to the wh-variable or explanans

competency_questions.question: Why must open-type answers carry a mandatory evidential warrant and when is warrant waived?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WARRANT_REQ mandates warrant or an explicit defeasibility marker for open-type answers

competency_questions.question: How is entailment between questions defined and how are questions soundly evoked by declaratives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QENTAILMENT defines refinement-based erotetic implication; EROTETIC_INFERENCE states evocation soundness

competency_questions.question: How is the question situated in discourse and decomposed into sub-questions whose answers compose?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUD situates the question; SUBQUESTION decomposes it so sub-answers compose to a parent answer

competency_questions.question: How do presuppositions project and how do interrogative complements compose under embedding predicates at the selected exhaustivity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRESUP_PROJECTION handles projection/filtering; EMBEDDED_Q composes the complement at the predicate-selected exhaustivity

glossary.definition: a canonical minimal proposition that fully and exactly resolves the question (a nuclear answer)
a proposition entailed by every direct answer; it must hold for the question to have a true answer
a question carrying a false or contestable presupposition, so no plain answer is true (a complex question)
a mention-all answer that settles, for every element, whether it falls under the question
an answer giving at least one true witness, sufficient for a mention-some question
the equivalence relation on worlds that groups worlds sharing the same complete true answer
the relation by which complete answers to one question yield complete answers to another
the question currently at issue in a discourse that governs relevance and accommodation
the relation by which a set of declaratives gives rise to (soundly poses) a question
an answer's instantiation of the wh-variable (or explanans) with an object of the correct sort/category

nodes.definition: Classify a question as polar (yes/no): a question whose logical form is a single proposition p offered for affirmation or denial, so its core answer space is the two-cell set {p, not-p} (optionally with 'unknown').

base.update_signal: polar-question grammar or yes/no answer-space convention is revised

pros.claim: Polar typing fixes a minimal, decidable answer space {p, not-p}, making answerhood mechanically checkable
pros.example: 'Is the door closed?' has direct answers 'yes (closed)' / 'no (not closed)'

cons.claim: Surface yes/no form can mask an alternative or biased question, mis-typing it as plain polar
cons.example: 'Did you stop lying?' is polar in form but carries a loaded presupposition

failure_modes: treating a tag/bias question as neutral polar
collapsing 'unknown' into a forced yes/no
acceptance_tests: the underlying proposition p is extracted and the answer space is exactly {p, not-p}(+unknown)
revisit_triggers: a polar surface masks alternatives or bias

nodes.definition: Classify a question as wh/constituent: a question built from an open sentence with one or more wh-variables (who/what/where/when/which) whose answers instantiate those variables; its answer space is the set of instances satisfying the matrix.

base.update_signal: wh-variable inventory or constituent-question schema changes

pros.claim: Representing a wh-question as a lambda-abstract over its matrix makes the set of instantiating answers explicit
pros.example: 'Who came?' = lambda-x.came(x); answers are the people who came

cons.claim: Multiple or nested wh-variables (pair-list, functional readings) explode the answer space and resist a single schema
cons.example: 'Which student read which book?' yields pair-list answers

failure_modes: ignoring the sortal restriction on the wh-variable
conflating single-wh and multiple-wh readings
acceptance_tests: each wh-variable and its sortal restriction is identified and the answer matrix is well-formed
revisit_triggers: a multiple/functional wh reading is observed

nodes.definition: Classify a question as alternative (disjunctive): a question presenting a closed list of mutually-exclusive, jointly-relevant options ('Tea or coffee?'), whose answers select exactly one (or a stated subset) of the listed alternatives.

base.update_signal: the enumerated alternative set or exclusivity convention changes

pros.claim: An alternative question fixes a finite closed option set, so its admissible answers are exactly the listed alternatives
pros.example: 'Stairs or elevator?' admits 'stairs' / 'elevator', not 'yes'

cons.claim: Disjunctive surface is ambiguous between a polar reading ('do you want either?') and a true alternative reading
cons.example: 'Tea or coffee?' may be answered 'yes' under a polar intonation

failure_modes: mis-reading an alternative question as polar
an alternative list that is not jointly exhaustive of the relevant space
acceptance_tests: the closed alternative list is enumerated and exactly-one-of selection is the answer form

nodes.definition: Classify a question as a why/explanation question: a question requesting an explanans for a presupposed explanandum (a fact taken as holding), whose answers are explanatory accounts relative to a contrast class, not mere instances.

base.update_signal: explanation model or contrast-class convention changes

included: the contrast class ('why P rather than Q')

pros.claim: Modeling a why-question with an explicit contrast class (van Fraassen) makes 'a good answer' relative and checkable
pros.example: 'Why did the bridge fail?' = rather than stand, asks for the failure-relevant cause

cons.claim: Explanatory relevance is theory-laden; what counts as an adequate explanans is not fixed by logical form alone
cons.example: causal vs functional vs intentional explanations all 'answer' the same why

failure_modes: answering a why-question with a restatement of the explanandum
ignoring the contrast class so the explanans is irrelevant
acceptance_tests: the explanandum and its contrast class are identified and answers are explanatory, not instantial

nodes.definition: Extract the presuppositions of a question: the propositions that must be true for the question to have any (true) direct answer at all, including the existential/uniqueness presuppositions carried by its wh-variables and definite terms.

base.update_signal: presupposition-projection theory or trigger inventory changes

pros.claim: A question's presupposition set is the entailment shared by all its direct answers (Belnap & Steel), making it computable from the answer space
pros.example: 'Who solved it?' presupposes someone solved it

cons.claim: Some presuppositions are defeasible or context-sensitive, so a fixed extraction can over- or under-generate
cons.example: 'When did you arrive?' presupposes arrival, cancellable by 'if you arrived'

failure_modes: missing a uniqueness presupposition on a singular wh
treating a cancellable implicature as a hard presupposition
acceptance_tests: the question's presupposition set is extracted and equals the common entailment of its direct answers
revisit_triggers: a defeasible presupposition is mis-classified as hard

nodes.definition: Detect when a question carries a presupposition that is false or contestable in the context (a loaded or complex question) and FLAG it rather than answering: a question with a false presupposition has no true direct answer and must be rejected/corrected, not answered yes or no.

base.update_signal: false-presupposition policy or contestation threshold changes

included: checking each presupposition against the common ground

pros.claim: Flagging a false presupposition blocks the trap of a forced yes/no that concedes the false proposition (the classic loaded question)
pros.example: 'Have you stopped cheating?' is flagged, not answered, when cheating never occurred

cons.claim: Over-flagging treats every contestable background as a false presupposition, refusing answerable questions
cons.example: flagging 'which exit did you take?' when an exit is in fact common ground

failure_modes: answering a loaded question and thereby conceding its false presupposition
silently repairing instead of surfacing the false presupposition
acceptance_tests: any question with a presupposition false-in-context is flagged with the offending presupposition, not answered
revisit_triggers: a loaded question is answered instead of flagged

nodes.definition: Define answerhood: the conditions under which a proposition counts as an answer to the question at all (resolving the question's issue), independent of whether it is true; this fixes what objects the question's semantics ranges over.

base.update_signal: answerhood criterion or resolvedness definition changes

pros.claim: A precise answerhood relation (Hamblin: a question denotes its set of possible answers) makes the question's meaning the set it partitions
pros.example: Hamblin's postulate: knowing the meaning of a question is knowing what counts as an answer

cons.claim: Multiple answerhood notions (resolving vs partial vs relevant) compete and a single choice under-serves some uses
cons.example: a partially-informative reply may 'answer' pragmatically but not resolve

failure_modes: admitting an off-issue proposition as an answer
equating answerhood with truth
acceptance_tests: the answerhood relation is fixed so that exactly the issue-resolving propositions qualify as answers
revisit_triggers: a partial/relevant-answer notion must be added

nodes.definition: Construct the set of direct answers: the canonical, minimal propositions that each fully and exactly resolve the question (Belnap & Steel's nuclear answers), one per cell of the question's issue, forming the semantic backbone of the question.

base.update_signal: direct-answer canonicalization rule changes

included: one canonical answer per issue cell
minimality / exactness of each direct answer

pros.claim: A fixed direct-answer set gives the question a determinate denotation against which every reply is measured
pros.example: 'Is it raining?' has direct answers {it is raining, it is not raining}

cons.claim: For open wh-questions the direct-answer set can be infinite, requiring a schema rather than an enumeration
cons.example: 'Which integer?' has unbounded direct answers

failure_modes: omitting a direct answer (incomplete answer space)
admitting a non-minimal/over-complete proposition as 'direct'
acceptance_tests: each direct answer is canonical and minimal, and the set covers every cell of the question's issue
revisit_triggers: an infinite direct-answer set must be schematized

nodes.definition: Distinguish complete from partial answers and the mention-some vs mention-all reading: a complete answer settles the whole issue (mention-all / strongly exhaustive), a partial answer settles part of it, and mention-some questions are satisfied by any single true witness.

base.update_signal: exhaustivity convention (mention-some vs mention-all) changes

pros.claim: Separating mention-some from mention-all sets the right adequacy bar per question and prevents demanding exhaustivity where one witness suffices
pros.example: 'Where can I buy coffee?' (mention-some) is answered by one cafe

cons.claim: The mention-some/mention-all reading is often underdetermined by surface form, so the wrong adequacy bar can be applied
cons.example: 'Who can chair?' is ambiguous between one eligible person and all of them

failure_modes: demanding mention-all where mention-some suffices
accepting a partial answer as if it were complete
acceptance_tests: the question's exhaustivity reading (some/all) is fixed and the completeness bar matches it

nodes.definition: Model a question as a partition of logical space (Groenendijk & Stokhof): the question's meaning is the equivalence relation on possible worlds that groups worlds giving the same complete true answer; each block is one strongly-exhaustive answer.

base.update_signal: partition vs alternative (Hamblin) semantics choice changes

pros.claim: Partition semantics makes question entailment a refinement relation between partitions, giving a clean algebra of questions
pros.example: a finer partition (more wh-variables) entails a coarser one

cons.claim: Strict partitions force strong exhaustivity and a complete cover, which is intractable for large/infinite world spaces and excludes mention-some
cons.example: partitioning over an infinite domain is not finitely representable

failure_modes: assuming a finite partition where the space is infinite
forcing mention-some questions into an exhaustive partition
acceptance_tests: the question induces a well-defined partition (equivalence relation) whose blocks are the exhaustive answers
revisit_triggers: an infinite or mention-some case breaks the partition assumption

nodes.definition: Compute the admissible answer set for closed question types (polar and alternative): the small, finite, exhaustively enumerable set of permitted answers, against which any reply is checked for membership; non-members are inadmissible by construction.

base.update_signal: closed-type admissible-set construction rule changes

pros.claim: For closed types the admissible set is finite and decidable, so answerhood is a simple membership check
pros.example: a polar question admits exactly {yes/p, no/not-p, unknown}

cons.claim: A rigid admissible set rejects an informative reply that resolves the issue in non-listed words
cons.example: 'half-open' truthfully answers 'Is the door closed?' but is not in {yes,no}

failure_modes: a reply outside the admissible set silently accepted
admissible set not jointly exhaustive of the issue
acceptance_tests: the closed-type admissible set is finite, exhaustive, and every reply is decided by membership
revisit_triggers: an informative non-listed reply must be accommodated

nodes.definition: Check type-conformance for open question types (wh, why): a reply must instantiate the wh-variable with an object of the correct sort (or supply an explanans of the right category for why), since open types have no finite admissible list, only a type/sort constraint.

base.update_signal: sortal-typing or category-matching rule for answers changes

included: sortal match of the answer to the wh-variable

pros.claim: Type-conformance replaces an impossible enumeration with a checkable sortal constraint for open questions
pros.example: 'Who came?' rejects 'at noon' (a time, not a person) as type-nonconforming

cons.claim: Sortal boundaries are fuzzy; coercion and metonymy let a type-mismatched surface answer be acceptable
cons.example: 'Who is the 9:15?' answered by a train number via metonymy

failure_modes: accepting a category-mismatched answer
over-strict sorting that rejects a coerced but valid answer
acceptance_tests: every accepted open-type answer instantiates the wh-variable/explanans with the correct sort or category
revisit_triggers: a metonymic/coerced answer challenges the sort check

nodes.definition: Require a mandatory evidential warrant for open-type answers: because an open answer asserts a contingent instance (who/what/why), it must come with or be defeasible by grounds; a type-conforming but unwarranted answer is admissible-in-form yet not acceptable-as-asserted.

base.update_signal: evidential-warrant requirement or defeasibility policy changes

included: warrant attachment to the asserted instance

pros.claim: Demanding warrant for open answers blocks confident-but-groundless instantiations of who/what/why
pros.example: 'Smith did it' is type-conforming but rejected without evidence linking Smith

cons.claim: A blanket warrant requirement can over-burden genuinely a-priori or definitional answers that need no empirical grounds
cons.example: 'Who is the bachelor's spouse?' needs no evidence: it is unwarranted by definition

failure_modes: accepting a groundless instantiation
demanding empirical warrant for a definitional answer
acceptance_tests: every open-type answer either carries a warrant or is explicitly marked defeasible/ungrounded
revisit_triggers: a definitional answer is wrongly required to carry empirical warrant

nodes.definition: Define entailment between questions: question Q1 erotetically implies Q2 when every complete answer to Q1 yields a complete answer to Q2 (Q1's partition refines Q2's), capturing when answering one settles another.

base.update_signal: erotetic-implication definition or refinement criterion changes

pros.claim: Question entailment lets a compiler reduce a question to an already-answered finer one, avoiding redundant inquiry
pros.example: answering 'who and when?' settles 'who?'

cons.claim: Refinement-based entailment is strict (mention-all); it misses pragmatic reductions that hold only mention-some
cons.example: a mention-some 'where to eat' is not entailed by the exhaustive list under strict refinement

failure_modes: claiming entailment where exhaustivity assumptions differ
ignoring presupposition mismatch between the two questions
acceptance_tests: Q1 implies Q2 iff every complete answer to Q1 determines a complete answer to Q2 with compatible presuppositions
revisit_triggers: a mention-some reduction is needed but refinement is strict

nodes.definition: Model erotetic inference (Wisniewski): how a question is evoked by a set of declaratives or arises from another question plus declaratives, with criteria of soundness (the evoked question is sound and its answers are relevant) for question-generating inferences.

base.update_signal: evocation/erotetic-implication soundness criteria change

included: evocation of a question by declaratives

pros.claim: Inferential erotetic logic gives a calculus for which questions legitimately arise, driving principled follow-up inquiry
pros.example: from 'exactly one suspect lied' evoke 'which suspect lied?'

cons.claim: Evocation criteria can license many sound questions, needing a relevance/utility filter to be operational
cons.example: a sound but useless question is evoked alongside the relevant one

failure_modes: evoking a question whose presupposition the premises do not secure
missing the relevance condition on the evoked question
acceptance_tests: each evoked/implied question is sound w.r.t. its premises and its presupposition is entailed by them
revisit_triggers: an irrelevant sound question must be filtered

nodes.definition: Place the question in the discourse as a Question Under Discussion (Roberts): the current QUD constrains relevance, accommodation, and which answers are felicitous, and structures the discourse as a stack/tree of questions and their moves.

base.update_signal: QUD relevance/accommodation model changes

included: relevance of a move to the QUD

pros.claim: The QUD framework makes relevance and information-structure (focus) a function of the active question, organizing discourse coherence
pros.example: a focus pattern is licensed by the QUD it answers

cons.claim: Identifying the operative QUD is itself inferential and can be contested, so QUD-relative judgments inherit that uncertainty
cons.example: accommodating a QUD that the speaker did not intend mis-reads the discourse

failure_modes: assuming a single QUD where several are open
accommodating an unintended QUD
acceptance_tests: the operative QUD is identified and each move is judged relevant relative to it

nodes.definition: Represent subordination: a question Q' is a sub-question of Q when answering Q' is a step toward answering Q (Q' is entailed by or refines part of Q under the QUD), yielding the question's decomposition into a strategy of inquiry.

base.update_signal: subordination criterion or strategy-of-inquiry model changes

included: decomposition of a question into a strategy

pros.claim: Subordination decomposes a hard question into answerable sub-questions, structuring inquiry as a tree
pros.example: 'who won and by how much?' subordinates 'who won?' then 'by how much?'

cons.claim: A wrong subordination can decompose into sub-questions whose answers do not recombine into a complete answer to the parent
cons.example: answering two sub-questions may still leave the parent's issue open

failure_modes: sub-questions whose answers do not compose to the parent answer
circular subordination between questions
acceptance_tests: each sub-question is entailed by or refines the parent and their answers compose to a parent answer

nodes.definition: Handle presupposition projection: determine which presuppositions of an embedded question survive (project) to the matrix and which are filtered, when a question is embedded under predicates ('knows whether', 'wonders who') or operators.

base.update_signal: projection theory or embedding-predicate inventory changes

pros.claim: Tracking projection prevents wrongly attributing an embedded question's presupposition to the speaker of the matrix
pros.example: 'Bob wonders who solved it' does not commit the matrix speaker to someone solving it

cons.claim: Projection behavior varies by predicate and is theory-dependent, so a single projection rule mis-predicts some embeddings
cons.example: 'knows who' (factive) projects existence; 'wonders who' may not

failure_modes: projecting a presupposition that the predicate filters
failing to project a factive presupposition
acceptance_tests: the embedded presuppositions that project vs are filtered are correctly assigned per embedding predicate
revisit_triggers: a new embedding predicate's behavior is observed

nodes.definition: Analyze negative/biased questions: questions whose form (high vs low negation, tag questions, 'really') signals a prior epistemic bias toward a particular answer, distinguishing the encoded bias from the neutral propositional content.

base.update_signal: bias taxonomy or negation-placement analysis changes

included: separation of bias from propositional content

pros.claim: Separating encoded bias from content prevents the bias from being read as a hard presupposition while still recording the speaker's lean
pros.example: 'Isn't the door closed?' biases toward 'closed' without presupposing it

cons.claim: The boundary between a strong bias and a genuine (loaded) presupposition is gradient and easy to over-read
cons.example: 'Didn't you cheat?' may be biased, or may presuppose cheating, depending on context

failure_modes: reading bias as a hard presupposition
ignoring bias and treating a biased question as neutral
acceptance_tests: the question's encoded bias is recorded separately from its neutral propositional content and answer space
revisit_triggers: bias is conflated with a hard presupposition

nodes.definition: Give the semantics of embedded/indirect questions: how an interrogative complement ('knows who came', 'asked whether p') composes with its embedding predicate, including the exhaustivity (weak/strong) the predicate imposes on the embedded answer.

base.update_signal: embedding-predicate semantics or exhaustivity selection changes

pros.claim: Compositional embedded-question semantics predicts whether 'knows who' demands strong or weak exhaustivity, fixing the truth conditions of the matrix
pros.example: 'knows who came' (strongly exhaustive) is false if Bob is missed

cons.claim: Predicates vary in the exhaustivity they select and some are ambiguous, so a uniform rule mis-predicts truth conditions
cons.example: 'agree on who' may take a weaker exhaustivity than 'know who'

failure_modes: assigning the wrong exhaustivity to the embedding predicate
treating a rogative predicate as responsive (or vice versa)
acceptance_tests: the interrogative complement composes with the predicate at the exhaustivity the predicate selects
revisit_triggers: a predicate's selected exhaustivity is mis-assigned

edges.risk_of_conflict: inconsistency if uncoordinated

edges.resolution_rule: select the exhaustivity bar from the question's reading and the embedding predicate: demand mention-all only when the form or predicate is strongly exhaustive; otherwise accept a mention-some witness as a full answer
edges.why_related: mention-some adequacy conflicts with mention-all (strongly exhaustive) adequacy for the same surface question
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the analysis

edges.resolution_rule: route by question type: closed types (polar/alternative) are decided by strict admissible-set membership; open types (wh/why) are decided by sortal type-conformance plus warrant, never by enumeration
edges.why_related: the strict finite admissible-set test for closed types conflicts with the open-ended type-conformance test for open types
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the analysis

edges.resolution_rule: if any presupposition is false-in-context, suppress the direct-answer selection and emit a presupposition-denying corrective (flag); only when all presuppositions hold may a direct answer be returned
edges.why_related: answering a question (returning a direct answer) conflicts with flagging it when its presupposition is false
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the analysis

edges.resolution_rule: use the full partition only when the world space is finite and exhaustivity is required; for tractability and for closed/mention-some cases, operate over the finite admissible set or a coarsening instead of the full partition
edges.why_related: partition completeness (a total exhaustive cover of logical space) conflicts with the tractability of a small finite admissible set
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the analysis

conflict_axes.name: mention_some_vs_mention_all_adequacy
conflict_axes.description: Mention-some accepts one true witness while mention-all demands a strongly exhaustive answer; the same surface question can take either reading.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read exhaustivity off the question form and the embedding predicate before setting the bar

conflict_axes.name: strict_admissible_set_vs_open_type_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Closed types decide answerhood by finite membership; open types have no finite list and need sortal type-conformance.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route closed types to admissible-set membership and open types to type-conformance plus warrant

conflict_axes.name: answering_vs_flagging_false_presupposition
conflict_axes.description: A loaded question invites a direct answer that concedes a false presupposition; flagging refuses to answer until the presupposition is corrected.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: check presuppositions first; flag and correct if any is false-in-context, otherwise answer

conflict_axes.name: partition_completeness_vs_tractability
conflict_axes.description: A complete partition of logical space is semantically clean but infeasible over large or infinite world spaces.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the partition for finite exhaustive cases; coarsen to a finite admissible set otherwise

conflict_axes.name: hard_presupposition_vs_encoded_bias
conflict_axes.description: A negative/biased question may merely lean toward an answer or may actually presuppose it; the boundary is gradient.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat as bias unless the proposition is entailed by every direct answer in context

conflict_axes.name: logical_answerhood_vs_evidential_acceptability
conflict_axes.description: A reply can satisfy logical answerhood (right form/type) yet be unacceptable as an unwarranted assertion.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: separate admissibility-in-form from acceptability-as-asserted; require warrant for the latter on open types

conflict_axes.name: strict_refinement_vs_pragmatic_reduction
conflict_axes.description: Erotetic implication via partition refinement is strict (mention-all) and misses pragmatic mention-some reductions between questions.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use refinement for guaranteed reductions; allow pragmatic reductions only under a stated exhaustivity reading

conflict_axes.name: projection_default_vs_predicate_specific
conflict_axes.description: A uniform presupposition-projection default mis-predicts embeddings that are predicate-specific (factive vs non-factive).
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply a default but override per embedding predicate's lexical projection profile

conflict_axes.name: single_qud_vs_multiple_open_questions
conflict_axes.description: Assuming one operative QUD simplifies relevance judgments but mis-reads discourses with several open questions.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: identify the QUD stack/tree; judge relevance against the topmost compatible question

edge_cases.description: A loaded question forces a yes/no whose either answer concedes a false presupposition.
edge_cases.trigger: a presupposition is false-in-context but the question is polar in form
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the false presupposition and emit a corrective instead of yes/no

edge_cases.description: A wh-question with no instances ('which unicorn?') has an unsatisfied existential presupposition, so no direct answer is true.
edge_cases.trigger: the existential presupposition of a wh-question fails
edge_cases.mitigation: detect the failed existential presupposition and report 'no such instance' rather than an empty answer

edge_cases.description: A disjunctive surface ('tea or coffee?') is answered 'yes', revealing a polar/alternative reading mismatch.
edge_cases.trigger: alternative question intoned or read as polar
edge_cases.mitigation: disambiguate by intonation/context before fixing the admissible set

edge_cases.description: A mention-some question ('where can I get coffee?') is wrongly held to a mention-all standard, rejecting a correct single witness.
edge_cases.trigger: strong-exhaustivity bar applied to a mention-some reading
edge_cases.mitigation: set the exhaustivity bar from the reading; accept one witness for mention-some

edge_cases.description: An open wh-question's direct-answer set is infinite ('which real number?'), so enumeration is impossible.
edge_cases.trigger: the wh-variable ranges over an infinite domain
edge_cases.mitigation: schematize the answer set and check sortal type-conformance instead of enumerating

edge_cases.description: A type-conforming answer ('Smith did it') is asserted with no grounds, satisfying form but not acceptability.
edge_cases.trigger: open-type answer lacks any evidential warrant
edge_cases.mitigation: require a warrant or an explicit defeasible/ungrounded marker before acceptance

edge_cases.description: A category-mismatched reply ('at noon' to 'who came?') is mistaken for an answer.
edge_cases.trigger: reply instantiates the wh-variable with the wrong sort
edge_cases.mitigation: reject sort-mismatched replies unless a coercion/metonymy is licensed

edge_cases.description: A presupposition of an embedded question is wrongly attributed to the matrix speaker.
edge_cases.trigger: non-projecting embedded presupposition treated as projecting
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the embedding predicate's projection profile (e.g. factive 'know' vs 'wonder')

edge_cases.description: A biased question ('isn't the door closed?') is read as presupposing 'closed' rather than merely leaning toward it.
edge_cases.trigger: encoded bias conflated with a hard presupposition
edge_cases.mitigation: record bias separately; treat as presupposition only if entailed by every direct answer

edge_cases.description: An embedding predicate's selected exhaustivity is mis-assigned, giving wrong truth conditions for 'knows who'.
edge_cases.trigger: weak exhaustivity applied where the predicate selects strong (or vice versa)
edge_cases.mitigation: assign exhaustivity from the predicate's lexical profile (responsive/rogative, weak/strong)

edge_cases.description: A claimed question entailment fails because the two questions carry incompatible presuppositions.
edge_cases.trigger: refinement asserted without checking presupposition compatibility
edge_cases.mitigation: require presupposition compatibility as a side condition on erotetic implication

edge_cases.description: Sub-questions are answered but their answers do not recombine into a complete answer to the parent question.
edge_cases.trigger: a decomposition whose sub-answers do not compose
edge_cases.mitigation: require the sub-question set to jointly entail a parent answer before decomposing

workflow.description: Classify the question as polar, alternative, wh, or why and fix the corresponding answer space.
workflow.gate: a single logical type and its answer space are assigned

workflow.description: Extract the presupposition set as the common entailment of the direct answers, including existential/uniqueness presuppositions.
workflow.gate: every direct answer entails the listed presuppositions

workflow.description: Test each presupposition against the common ground; if any is false-in-context, flag and stop rather than answer.
workflow.gate: no presupposition is false-in-context, or the question is flagged

workflow.description: Fix the answerhood relation: which propositions resolve the question's issue.
Build the canonical minimal direct-answer set covering each cell of the issue.
workflow.gate: the direct answers cover the issue and are minimal

workflow.description: Determine the mention-some vs mention-all reading and the complete/partial boundary.
workflow.gate: the exhaustivity bar matches the question reading

workflow.description: Model the question as a partition for finite exhaustive cases, or coarsen to a finite admissible set for closed/tractable cases.
workflow.gate: a partition or finite admissible set is well-defined

workflow.description: For polar/alternative questions, decide answers by membership in the finite admissible set.
workflow.gate: each reply is decided by admissible-set membership

workflow.description: For wh/why questions, check sortal/category conformance of the reply to the wh-variable or explanans.
Require an evidential warrant (or explicit defeasibility marker) for each open-type answer.
workflow.gate: every open answer carries warrant or a defeasibility marker

workflow.description: For embedded questions, project/filter presuppositions and compose the complement at the predicate-selected exhaustivity.
workflow.gate: projection and exhaustivity follow the embedding predicate

workflow.description: Place the question as the QUD and, if needed, decompose it into sub-questions whose answers compose.
workflow.gate: the QUD is identified and any sub-questions compose to a parent answer

dominance_rules.rule: FALSE_PRESUP must run and clear before DIRECT_ANSWER may return any answer
dominance_rules.rationale: a question with a false presupposition has no true direct answer; answering concedes the false proposition
dominance_rules.trigger: answer selection begins with an unchecked or failed presupposition
dominance_rules.action: block answering; flag the false presupposition and emit a corrective

dominance_rules.rule: The question's logical type (QTYPE_*) must be fixed before answerhood and admissibility are computed
dominance_rules.rationale: the answer space and admissibility test are determined by the question type
dominance_rules.trigger: answerhood computed before the type is assigned

dominance_rules.rule: Closed types are decided by ADMISSIBLE_SET membership; open types by TYPE_CONFORMANCE, never by enumeration
dominance_rules.rationale: open types have no finite admissible list, only a sortal constraint
dominance_rules.trigger: an open wh-question is forced into a finite admissible enumeration
dominance_rules.action: route open types to type-conformance plus warrant

dominance_rules.rule: The exhaustivity reading (mention-some vs mention-all) must be fixed before completeness is judged
dominance_rules.rationale: the completeness bar depends on the reading and the embedding predicate
dominance_rules.trigger: a completeness judgment without a fixed exhaustivity reading
dominance_rules.action: set the reading from form/predicate before judging completeness

dominance_rules.rule: Open-type answers require a warrant before acceptance-as-asserted
dominance_rules.rationale: a type-conforming answer can still be a groundless assertion
dominance_rules.trigger: an open answer accepted with no warrant or defeasibility marker
dominance_rules.action: require warrant or mark the answer defeasible

dominance_rules.rule: Erotetic implication (QENTAILMENT) requires presupposition compatibility as a side condition
dominance_rules.rationale: refinement alone can relate questions whose presuppositions clash
dominance_rules.action: add presupposition compatibility to the implication check

dominance_rules.rule: Embedded-question presuppositions project per the embedding predicate's profile, not by a blanket rule
dominance_rules.rationale: factive and non-factive predicates project differently
dominance_rules.trigger: a uniform projection default applied across all predicates
dominance_rules.action: override the default with the predicate's projection profile

dominance_rules.rule: Use the full PARTITION_SEM only for finite exhaustive cases; otherwise coarsen to a finite admissible set
dominance_rules.rationale: a complete partition is intractable over infinite world spaces
dominance_rules.trigger: a partition attempted over an infinite or very large world space
dominance_rules.action: coarsen to a finite admissible set or schema

dominance_rules.rule: Encoded bias (NEGATIVE_QUESTION) must not narrow the neutral admissible answer space
dominance_rules.rationale: bias records the speaker's lean, not a restriction on what answers are admissible
dominance_rules.trigger: a biased question's admissible set narrowed to the favored answer
dominance_rules.action: keep the neutral answer space; record bias separately

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not select a direct answer before clearing presuppositions; a later false-presupposition finding invalidates the answer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting an answer that conceded a false presupposition

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not compute answerhood before fixing the question type; a re-typing forces recomputation of the answer space
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recomputing the entire answer space after a late re-typing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not enumerate an admissible set for an open wh-question; the unbounded list must be rebuilt as a schema
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discarding an infinite enumeration and re-deriving a sortal schema

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not judge completeness before fixing the mention-some/mention-all reading; the wrong bar must be redone
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-grading every answer after the exhaustivity reading flips

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not accept an open-type answer before warrant; an unwarranted answer admitted now is re-litigated later
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-opening accepted answers to attach missing warrants

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not assert question entailment without checking presupposition compatibility; clashes surface downstream
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding a reduction built on incompatible presuppositions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not apply a blanket presupposition-projection rule across embedding predicates; predicate-specific cases must be redone
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reanalyzing every embedded question after a projection misprediction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not build a full partition over an unbounded world space; an intractable model must be coarsened and rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the semantic model after a partition proves infeasible

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not conflate encoded bias with a hard presupposition; misclassifying it forces re-judging answerhood
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-deriving the answer space after a bias was mistaken for a presupposition

iteration_protocol.trigger: a question with a false presupposition was answered yes/no instead of flagged
iteration_protocol.action: strengthen presupposition checking in PRESUPPOSITION and the flag/correct path in FALSE_PRESUP before answer selection

iteration_protocol.trigger: a mention-some question was rejected for failing a mention-all bar
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the exhaustivity reading in COMPLETE_ANSWER and re-set the bar in ANSWERHOOD

iteration_protocol.trigger: an open wh-question was forced into a finite admissible enumeration
iteration_protocol.action: route it through TYPE_CONFORMANCE and schematize the answer set instead of enumerating

iteration_protocol.trigger: a type-conforming answer was accepted with no grounds
iteration_protocol.action: enforce the warrant requirement in WARRANT_REQ before acceptance-as-asserted

iteration_protocol.trigger: an embedded question's presupposition was attributed to the matrix speaker
iteration_protocol.action: apply the predicate-specific projection profile in PRESUP_PROJECTION and re-compose in EMBEDDED_Q

iteration_protocol.trigger: a claimed question entailment broke on incompatible presuppositions
iteration_protocol.action: add the presupposition-compatibility side condition to QENTAILMENT and re-check EROTETIC_INFERENCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a partition was attempted over an infinite world space
iteration_protocol.action: coarsen PARTITION_SEM to a finite admissible set in ADMISSIBLE_SET

iteration_protocol.trigger: sub-question answers did not compose into a parent answer
iteration_protocol.action: require joint entailment of a parent answer in SUBQUESTION before decomposing under the QUD

priority_rationale: question typing (QTYPE_*) and presupposition extraction are foundational; FALSE_PRESUP gates answering; answerhood, direct answers and completeness fix the answer space; admissible-set vs type-conformance/warrant split closed from open types; partition semantics, erotetic implication, QUD, subordination and embedding close the analysis.
